A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ProDe, with matching core methods and experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and sufficiently complete for comparison, including Appendices A-D in v1 and A-F in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original adaptation experiments on Office-31, Office-Home, VisDA, and DomainNet-126, together with component ablations, feature visualizations, and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original ProDe experiments and adds multi-target, multi-source, test-time adaptation, OpenCLIP, prompt-initialization, and computational-cost results.

M1.justification: The core logit correction, mutual-information and pseudo-label objective, and Algorithm 1 remain equivalent; LSyn is renamed LApt. A limited procedural extension appears in Section 4.2: ProDe-V-Ens averages predictions from separately adapted source models for multi-source adaptation.

E1.justification: The four datasets are retained, but v2 adds Office-Home evaluations with multiple target domains, multiple source models, and online test-time adaptation (Tables 7 and 15). These substantially extend the task and data-access conditions beyond v1's closed-set, partial-set, open-set, and generalized SFDA evaluations.

E2.justification: v2 adds comparisons with CoNMix, SHOT-Ens, DECISION, Tent, T3A, CoTTA, EATA, and SAR in Table 7. It also adds DIFO-V16 to the existing backbone comparison, introduces ViT-based comparisons including DIPE-ViT, DSiT-ViT, and DPC in Table 10, and compares against OpenCLIP zero-shot results. The original benchmark comparator sets are largely retained.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include pooled target-domain training, multi-source ensemble evaluation, online adaptation with batch size 64, OpenCLIP substitution, and prompt-initialization controls. In retained analyses, the reported oracle training domain changes from Cl to Ar, and the sensitivity task changes from Cl-to-Ar to Ar-to-Cl; the PDFs do not establish whether these reflect corrections or reruns. The main SGD, epoch, batch-size, and hyperparameter settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds OpenCLIP reliance tests across four datasets, nine-template initialization sensitivity, and training-resource analysis (Tables 16-20, 22-23). Table 8 adds accuracy results for the KL-loss variant previously examined through adaptation trajectories. Existing component, prompt-learning, backbone, and parameter-sensitivity analyses are retained or revised rather than wholly new.

E5.justification: Both implementation appendices state that each transfer task is repeated five times and report the average. Neither version introduces experimental error bars, confidence intervals, significance tests, or additional seed information.

E6.justification: Corresponding tables substantially revise existing results: ProDe-V's Office-Home accuracy changes from 86.2 to 84.5 and VisDA accuracy from 91.6 to 91.0 (Table 2). Its generalized-SFDA H score changes from 85.1 to 84.8, falling below PSAT-ViT's unchanged 85.0 (Table 6). Numerous ablation and per-task results also change. New Table 7 reports averages of 83.6, 85.0, and 76.5 for multi-target, multi-source, and test-time adaptation, respectively.

T1.justification: v2 revises Equation 1 from a scalar-distance equality to a relation using vector lengths and the triangle inequality. This is a substantive mathematical correction, although limited in scope. Theorem 1's conclusion and the entropy-ratio argument in Appendix A remain essentially unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction extend the claimed superiority and applicability of ProDe to multi-target, multi-source, and test-time adaptation. This materially broadens the scope of the main empirical contribution beyond v1's four SFDA settings. The central novelty claims concerning proxy denoising, proxy confidence theory, and mutual distillation are retained.

C2.justification: v2 removes the offline/data-streaming limitation while retaining the white-box restriction. It adds substantive explanations concerning generalist versus specialist models, independence from a particular ViL model, prompt learning reducing proxy error, and computational efficiency. It also introduces an overfitting explanation for the Office-31 exception in the new ViT comparison. These broaden applicability and mechanism interpretations beyond v1.

D1.justification: The promised future code release becomes an explicit code-and-data repository link. v2 also documents tested prompt-initialization strings and per-iteration GPU-memory and training-time measurements. Most architecture, optimizer, training-budget, and hyperparameter information is retained from v1.

R1.justification: The existing SFDA and vision-language positioning is retained. v2 adds Xiao et al. alongside DIFO when discussing noisy ViL supervision, plus references supporting OpenCLIP, the Gaussian approximation, multi-domain adaptation, TTA, and newer ViT comparisons. The prototype-oriented work by Tanwisuth et al. is omitted. These extend the literature coverage without replacing the central positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and method explanations receive substantial rewriting. Algorithm 1 and dataset descriptions move into dedicated appendices, while the backbone comparison moves into the main text. References now precede the reorganized appendices. Terminology, author information, and acknowledgments also change.

P2.justification: The manuscript changes from a two-column format to the predominantly single-column ICLR layout. Tables are regrouped, the multimodal-indicator column is removed, and numerous new comparison and analysis tables appear. Figures 3 and 4 change from grids to horizontal panel arrangements, while Figures 4 and 5 have revised plots and axes.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens practical validation through tests of ViL dependence, prompt initialization, broader adaptation conditions, and computational cost, while adding concrete code/data access information. Reporting problems limit the net gain: Section 4.3 claims ProDe-V16 surpasses every comparator although Table 9 gives 86.9 versus DAMP-V16's 87.1 on Office-Home. The new OpenCLIP results also report conflicting Office-Home averages for ProDe, 89.6 in Table 17 and 90.3 in Table 20.
